reference: Independent python implementation of IEC 60909-0:2016 written from the standard's own equations - network feeder Z_Q = c U_nQ^2/S_kQ'' referred by the turns ratio, two-winding transformer Z_T/R_T/X_T with the 6.3.3 impedance correction factor K_T, cable impedance with the resistance temperature correction, asynchronous-motor locked-rotor impedance eq. (26), the equivalent voltage source c U_n/sqrt3 at the fault point solved as a slack node of the nodal admittance system, kappa eq. (56) and i_p eq. (55), the line-to-line relation eq. (34) and the IEC 60364-4-41 earth fault loop; the load flow is a scipy Newton solution of the complex nodal power balance, structurally different from the tool's backward/forward sweep. Every motor-free case is cross-checked against the analytic series path impedance Z = Z_source + sum(Z_branch), which is also verified by hand for case hand_single_feeder.
reference_citations: IEC 60909-0:2016, 6.1 eq. (3)-(5) - network feeder impedance Z_Q = c U_nQ^2/S_kQ'' and its referral Z_Qt = Z_Q/t_r^2
IEC 60909-0:2016, 6.2 eq. (7)-(9) - two-winding transformer Z_T = (u_kr/100) U_rT^2/S_rT, R_T = P_krT/(3 I_rT^2), X_T = sqrt(Z_T^2-R_T^2)
IEC 60909-0:2016, 6.3.3 - transformer impedance correction factor K_T = 0.95 c_max/(1+0.6 x_T)
IEC 60909-0:2016, 6.8 eq. (26) - asynchronous motor Z_M = (1/(I_LR/I_rM)) U_rM/(sqrt3 I_rM)
IEC 60909-0:2016, 4.2 eq. (29) - three-phase initial symmetrical current I_k'' = c U_n/(sqrt3 |Z_k|)
IEC 60909-0:2016, 4.2 eq. (34) - line-to-line current I_k2'' = c U_n/|Z_1+Z_2| = (sqrt3/2) I_k3'' when Z_2 = Z_1
IEC 60909-0:2016, Table 1 - voltage factor c for low voltage (c_max 1.05/1.10, c_min 0.95)
IEC 60364-4-41:2005, 411.4.4 - automatic disconnection in TN: Z_s I_a <= U_0, evaluated here as I_f = c_min U_0/|Z_s|
tolerance: Agreement to the last digit the page prints: |got-ref| <= 0.5*10^-d + 1e-9*|ref|, with d = 3 decimals for every kA/kappa figure in the selected-feeder panel, 2 decimals for current (A), voltage (V), voltage drop (%) and cable losses (kW), and 1 decimal for the source-current KPI. Both sides evaluate the same closed-form IEC 60909 expressions, so the only physical slack is double-precision round-off; the tolerance is set by the display, not by what makes the tool pass.

cases.note: Single 95 mm2 copper feeder, R20 pinned at 0.193 ohm/km, X 0.08 ohm/km, 630 kVA / 4 % transformer, KT off - the whole chain is a hand sum of three series impedances.
As above with the IEC 60909-0 6.3.3 transformer impedance correction factor KT = 0.95 cmax/(1+0.6 xT) enabled.
1000 kVA / 6 % transformer, cmax = 1.10, fault at the LV busbar: Ik is the transformer plus network-feeder impedance only.
180 m aluminium feeder; minimum-current case at 90 C conductor temperature exercises the resistance temperature correction.
Series bus + feeder: the driving-point impedance at the load is the sum of source, DB-1 feeder and load feeder impedances.
One 90 kW motor with ILR/Ir = 6 feeding a bus fault: the motor branch is a shunt impedance IEC 60909-0 eq. (26) in parallel with the network.
Two motors on separate feeders; fault at the LV busbar. Checks that the motor contribution is the parallel sum of both motor branches and that the static load contributes nothing.
Same network, fault at the terminals of motor M1: its own locked-rotor impedance is directly in parallel with the supply.
Four levels of radial cable; also exercises the load-flow voltage drop accumulated along the whole path.
Stiff 2 MVA / 6 % transformer on a 2 GVA feeder with X/R = 30: kappa is close to its 1.8-2.0 range and i_p is the dominant number.
Very small cable far from the transformer: R/X is large, kappa collapses towards 1.02 and Ik is set almost entirely by the cable resistance.
TN earth-fault loop: Zs is the upstream loop plus phase and PE conductor of every feeder on the path; If = cmin U0 / |Zs| (IEC 60364-4-41 411.4.4).

Load flow: a 110 kW motor (input power P/eta) and a 90 kW static load on one sub-board. Checks branch current, bus voltage, cumulative voltage drop, cable losses and the generation = load + losses balance.
Unity power factor, zero cable reactance: the voltage drop is exactly R*I and the losses are exactly 3 I^2 R.

Breaker instantaneous pickup at 8 In = 800 A is far below the fault current, so the clearing time is exactly t_i = 0.05 s and the adiabatic minimum section S = I sqrt(t)/k (IEC 60364-4-43 table 43A, k = 115 for PVC-insulated copper) can be checked in closed form.
TT system: the earth-fault loop is R_A + R_B plus the phase and PE conductors of the feeder, If = cmin U0/|Z| (IEC 60364-4-41 411.5).
TN loop with an explicitly chosen 50 mm2 aluminium PE conductor and its own reactance, so the PE branch of the loop is not the phase conductor.

environment: Chromium (Playwright) on Linux, file:// origin, ?lang=en. Reference generated by python 3 with numpy/scipy (bench-src/ref/gen_electricalnetwork.py).
not_benchmarked: The symmetrical breaking current Ib, the steady-state current Ik, the d.c. component i_DC and the m/n Joule-integral factors of IEC 60909-0 clause 4.5-4.8 - the tool does not compute them, so the motor contribution is benchmarked only as an initial symmetrical current I_kM'' with no decay.

Zero-sequence and negative-sequence networks: only the Z_2 = Z_1 line-to-line relation eq. (34) and the installation-level TN/TT earth-loop screening are exercised. IT systems are unsupported by the tool.
The current-carrying-capacity (Iz) tables and their correction factors, which the page shares with the Cable Sizing tool and which are benchmarked there.

The generic breaker time-current model (In/Isd/tsd/Ii/ti/t6) and the range-based selectivity screening: these are the page's own engineering model, not a standardised curve; only the case where the fault current exceeds the instantaneous pickup (clearing time = t_i exactly) is used, and only to check the adiabatic equation S = I sqrt(t)/k around it.

The conductor resistivity model (R20 = 18.56 Cu / 29.38 Al ohm mm2/km, alpha = 0.00393 / 0.00403 per K): every benchmark case pins R20 with the per-feeder override so the graded numbers do not depend on it. Note IEC 60909-0:2016 6.4 prescribes alpha = 0.004 1/K for copper and aluminium; the page uses the physical coefficients instead, a 0.15 % difference in R at 70 C.
crosscheck: Every motor-free case is computed twice: once by solving the equivalent-voltage-source network with the faulted node as a slack node, and once from the analytic series impedance Z = Z_source + sum(Z_branch) along the path. Worst mutual deviation over 15 cases: 1.27e-15 relative (double-precision round-off). Case hand_single_feeder is additionally verified by hand: |Z| = 20.641 mOhm, Ik'' = 11747.4 A, i_p = 17.881 kA.
power_balance_note: Load-flow invariant checked in the reference for every case: 3 Re(V_LV conj(I_root)) = sum(P_load/eta) + sum(3 |I|^2 R). Worst residual 1.66e-13 relative.
provenance_note: Every reference value is recomputed by bench-src/ref/gen_electricalnetwork.py from the sources this artifact cites; that generator was re-run against this tree on 2026-10-03 and its output compared with the deployed corpus leaf by leaf at 2 658 leaves, 0 differing, so no case reuses a stored ref and none carries ref_source "recorded".
